children.value: Self-paced, can be done in less than a week
The majority of turnover occurs in the first 90 days of employment.
CNAs have a great potential to help decrease turnover by serving as a teacher, mentor and coach for the newest members of your team.
This eight-module course is designed to equip CNAs with the tools necessary to serve as a bridge to help get the new staff through that critical phase of initial employment.
They can also assist students who are conducting clinical rotations in the facility.

Each is self-paced, can be done in less than a week
CNAs often report difficulty responding to resident behavior related to dementia or serious mental illness.
Providing CNAs with skills to identify and respond to issues involving resident dementia and mental health is critical, both to quality of care and to staff safety.
online training and certification programs provide CNAs with skills to identify and respond to issues and behaviors that may result in problems and appropriately deescalate them.
CNAs learn the CARES® 5-step method to respond to dementia-related behavior and challenging situations. CNAs may choose the dementia specialty or the behavioral health specialty.

inventory.text: CNA Upskilling Program (CUSP) Certifications CNA II Certified Preceptor Details 3 hour online training Self-paced, can be done in less than a week Concept The majority of turnover occurs in the first 90 days of employment. CNAs have a great potential to help decrease turnover by serving as a teacher, mentor and coach for the newest members of your team. This eight-module course is designed to equip CNAs with the tools necessary to serve as a bridge to help get the new staff through that critical phase of initial employment. They can also assist students who are conducting clinical rotations in the facility. CNA III Restorative Nurse Assistant Details 10 hours online, 6 hours in-person skills testing Concept RNA has existed informally in SNFs for ages. In 2005-2007, QCHF created a formal training program to professionalize these positions. CNA IV Behavioral Health or Dementia Specialty Details 8 hour online training each specialty (must complete one specialty for CUSP reimbursement) Each is self-paced, can be done in less than a week Incorporates a person-centered approach Courses provided by HealthCare Interactive, Inc. Concept CNAs often report difficulty responding to resident behavior related to dementia or serious mental illness. Providing CNAs with skills to identify and respond to issues involving resident dementia and mental health is critical, both to quality of care and to staff safety. HealthCare Interactive CARES® online training and certification programs provide CNAs with skills to identify and respond to issues and behaviors that may result in problems and appropriately deescalate them. CNAs learn the CARES® 5-step method to respond to dementia-related behavior and challenging situations. CNAs may choose the dementia specialty or the behavioral health specialty. CNAs may choose the dementia specialty or the behavioral health specialty. Testimonials Oak River Rehab “While the application process at first seemed a bit daunting, once the CNAP team walked me through everything, it was super easy to submit all of the required documents. From there on out, we only saw great benefits through our relationship with CNAP, including the care that our Earn and Learn CNA graduates are now delivering in our facility.” Chad Kanow , Assistant Administrator , Oak River Rehab Kern Valley “CNAP awards have allowed us to continue to offer this program with a reduced demand on facilities resources! It is very easy to work with the CNAP staff! The application process is simple, they explain everything, and it is well organized. We feel incredibly supported!” Brandy Arana, Administrator and NATP Coordinator, Kern Valley Crystal Ridge Care Center "Without knowing the process, the CNAP application can seem a bit daunting, but once you work with the CNAP team, the process is really streamlined, not complicated at all. The staff is so supportive." - Daenen Miller, Administrator, Crystal Ridge Care Center The Pines at Placerville "We just received our first check for the CNAP program for the 18 CNAs that we put through our CNA class. All our interactions with Mai and Zane have been nothing short of amazing. They were with us the entire way and felt invested in our success. Their instructions were clear and concise, and they went above and beyond to ensure we received our reward. We will gladly continue to work with them in future cohorts and are grateful for this partnership." - Colby Hollingsworth, Administrator Southern Inyo Healthcare District “We are thrilled with the CNAP funds received as they have provided us with the financial flexibility to enhance our classrooms and work stations for both our employee students and long-term staff. Thanks to CNAP we can invest in improvements that directly benefit our learning environment and support our educational goals. The process of accessing the funds was straightforward and we appreciate the opportunity to utilize them for our specific needs. CNAP has truly made a positive impact on our facility, and we look forward to our continued partnership.” -Jennifer Emley, Quality Assistant Fallbrook Skilled Nursing “Our experience with the CNAP program has been incredibly beneficial to our facility. With our second cohort of Earn and Learn students graduating soon and another one planned for the near future, CNAP has played a vital role in addressing our staffing needs. Thanks to the Earn and Learn classes, we have significantly reduced our reliance on the CNA registry, saving us $50,000 per month. CNAP’s support has empowered us to build a sustainable workforce and further enhance our patient care and satisfaction. We look forward to our continued partnership.” -Robert Durban, Administrator Golden Heights Healthcare “Thanks to the valuable guidance and support from CNAP staff and the CNAP Resources, our facility navigated the accreditation process and successfully obtained our facility based NATP approval. This achievement not only brought us multiple financial rewards but has also empowered us to hire and train our own CNAs. We are now eagerly preparing to launch an Earn and Learn program, with the goal of building a sustainable and renewable workforce.” -Almaroof Apatira, Administrator Kern Valley Healthcare District "CNAP has aided us with graduating 12 Nurse Assistant Students, successfully passing their state exams to obtain their certifications. The application process is simple and well organized. CNAP awards have allowed us to continue to offer this program with a reduced demand on facilities resources and has offered us a great deal more support than just financial awards. Earn and Learn helps increase our retention of newly trained and certified CNA’s!" -Brandy Arana, LMS Administrator and NATP Coordinator Compass Health, Inc. "Quality Care Health Foundation’s Certified Nursing Assistant Program has been a welcome resource in supporting our goals of training and retaining CNAs. The CNAP program team was easy to work with and supportive throughout the award application and disbursement process. They kept their requests concise, were realistic with deliverable due dates and sent reminders when needed." - Patrick Woolpert, Finance Director Cambridge Health Services "Our experience working with CNAP has been wonderful. Megan was clear and concise with all instructions and also easy to reach if I had any questions. I have felt supported throughout the entire process. As we endeavor to train the best CNAs to support our residents, this grant has made the process so much easier. The support has allowed us to continue to grow our program which only benefits our facilities and residents! We look forward to our future partnership with CNAP in the coming years!" - Jenny Rivera, Cambridge Health Services
